title: Exact class-group relations
objective: Implement exact relation admission/replay, smooth principal-ideal factorization, initial rational-prime relations, deterministic LLL relation search scaffolding, and focused tests

handoff.summary: Implemented an ordinary-Python exact relation layer with canonical factored principal-witness payloads, full source/quotient/principal ideal evidence, complete norm smoothness evidence, optional archimedean log payloads, deterministic provenance, independent replay, and component-mutation rejection. `RelationRecord.row` is the dense principal exponent row and `sparse_row()` returns zero-based nonzero entries for matrix consumers. `ExactRelationCollector` verifies before admission, incrementally screens rank modulo a prime, deduplicates exact records, and optionally forwards duck-typed records into `context.add_relation`. Rational-prime decomposition seeds are deterministic and admitted only when the complete decomposition lies in the factor base. The bounded LLL scaffold uses exact 3/4 reduction of coefficient lattices, Hecke-style basis/weight-two candidates, deterministic bounded combinations, missing-pivot-biased factor-base ideal products, and serializable xorshift state. The offline Sage/PARI and Hecke/Oscar fixture covers inert 2, ramified 5, a source-ideal uniformizer relation, signed fractional rows, nonsmooth rejection, five certificate corruptions, checkpoint/resume, and bounded replay. Focused runtime validation passes in about 10.4 seconds including 12 full replays; standalone pyright reports zero errors.
risks: The readable initial reducer is exact for the power-basis coefficient lattice, not yet a Minkowski/Arb-weighted lattice. `LLLRelationSearch.basis_reducer` is an explicit injection point for the production Minkowski reducer without changing certificates.

Smoothness currently computes exact valuations and reconstructs the ideal. It is correctness-first and will inherit the integration lane's cached prime-power/coordinate-inverse valuation acceleration; no duplicate fast valuation path is present here.

Archimedean logs and precision are retained with the frozen complex-place convention but are not used to certify exact ideal replay. The analytic/unit lane must recompute and validate them for regulator claims.
Large-prime partial matching and automorphism orbits remain future search accelerations. Nonsmooth candidates are rejected exactly rather than admitted heuristically.
The lane-required broad baselib strict and native receipts are intentionally pending per coordinator direction; central integration owns those gates and the transition from active to review.
next_steps: Integrate `RelationRecord` and `ExactRelationCollector` through the shared class/unit context using their duck-typed `add_relation`, `row`, `sparse_row`, `to_dict`, and `verify` surfaces.

Add the module to pyrightconfig.json and any public/test registries in the integration lane, then run and record `pnpm test:baselib:strict` and `pnpm test:native` before moving this contract to review.
Connect a Minkowski/Arb basis reducer and the integration lane's fast integral valuation cache, then benchmark cubic/quartic factor bases before selecting any native kernel.
Add exact one-large-prime partial combination and independently replayable automorphism-derived records once the deterministic small-field vertical slice is integrated.
